value.event: Sima Yu, Teng's son, drove Li Feng into the river and was killed by Feng's remnants.

kinshipTerm.en: Four sons survived: Yu, Jiao, Shao, Que

sentences.zh: 安平獻王孚

translations.literal: Prince Fu of Anping with posthumous title Xian (section heading).
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian of Anping, Sima Fu.

sentences.zh: 初，騰發并州，次於真定。

translations.literal: At first when Teng set out from Bing Province he halted at Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving Bing he paused at Zhending.

sentences.zh: 值大雪，平地數尺，營門前方數丈雪融不積，騰怪而掘之，得玉馬，高尺許，表獻之。

translations.literal: It happened there was great snow several chi deep on level ground; before the camp gate several zhang of ground showed melted snow not accumulating; Teng wondered and dug obtaining a jade horse about a chi high which he memorialized and presented.
translations.idiomatic: Snow melted oddly at his gate; digging revealed a jade horse sent to court.

sentences.zh: 其後公師籓與平陽人汲桑等為群盜，起於清河鄃縣，眾千餘人，寇頓丘，以葬成都王穎為辭，載穎主而行，與張泓故將李豐等將攻鄴。

translations.literal: Later duke-lord Shi Fan with Pingyang men Ji Sang and others formed bandit gangs rising in Shu county of Qinghe over one thousand strong raiding Dunqiu using burying Prince of Chengdu Ying as pretext loading Ying's spirit tablet marching with Zhang Hong's old general Li Feng intending to attack Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Sang's gang marched under Ying's tablet to threaten Ye.

sentences.zh: 騰曰：「孤在并州七年，胡圍城不能克。

translations.literal: Teng said, 'I was at Bing seven years and barbarians besieging the city could not overcome it.
translations.idiomatic: Teng said, 'I was at Bing seven years and barbarians besieging the city could not overcome it.

sentences.zh: 汲桑小賊，何足憂也。」

translations.literal: Ji Sang petty bandits—what worth worry.'
translations.idiomatic: Ji Sang petty bandits—what worth worry.'

sentences.zh: 及豐等至，騰不能守，率輕騎而走，為豐所害。

translations.literal: When Feng and others arrived Teng could not defend and led light horse fleeing and was killed by Feng.
translations.idiomatic: The raid overwhelmed him; fleeing lightly armed he fell to Feng.

sentences.zh: 四子：虞、矯、紹、確。

translations.literal: Four sons: Yu, Jiao, Shao, Que.
translations.idiomatic: Four sons survived: Yu, Jiao, Shao, Que.

sentences.zh: 虞有勇力，騰之被害，虞逐豐，豐投水而死。

translations.literal: Yu had courage and strength; when Teng was harmed Yu pursued Feng who threw himself in water and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yu avenged his father driving Feng into the river.

sentences.zh: 是日，虞及矯、紹並钜鹿太守崔曼、車騎長史羊恆、從事中郎蔡克等又為豐餘黨所害，及諸名家流移依鄴者，死亡並盡。

translations.literal: That same day Yu together with Jiao and Shao and Julu governor Cui Man chariot-and-cavalry chief clerk Yang Heng consultant Cai Ke were again harmed by Feng's remaining faction and renowned families taking refuge at Ye perished altogether.
translations.idiomatic: The bloodbath wiped Julu officials and refugee clans at Ye.

sentences.zh: 初，鄴中雖府庫虛竭，而騰資用甚饒。

translations.literal: At first though Ye granaries were exhausted Teng's private wealth was very ample.
translations.idiomatic: Ye's arsenals stood empty yet Teng hoarded wealth.

sentences.zh: 性儉嗇，無所振惠，臨急，乃賜將士米可數升，帛各丈尺，是以人不為用，遂致於禍。

translations.literal: By nature stingy he showed no generosity; facing crisis he then gifted officers several sheng of rice and bolts only one zhang therefore men would not serve him and ruin followed.
translations.idiomatic: His miserly handfuls of grain and cloth bought no loyalty and brought disaster.

sentences.zh: 及苟晞救鄴，桑還平陽。

translations.literal: When Gou Xi relieved Ye Sang returned to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Xi's relief sent Ji Sang back toward Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 于時盛夏，屍爛壞不可復識，騰及三子骸骨不獲。

translations.literal: It was then deep summer; corpses rotted beyond recognition and Teng's and his three sons' bones could not be recovered.
translations.idiomatic: It was midsummer, and the corpses had decayed beyond recognition; the remains of Teng and his three sons could not be recovered.

sentences.zh: 庶子確立。

translations.literal: His son by a secondary consort, Que, succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son by a secondary consort, Sima Que, succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 敬王恬，字元愉，少拜散騎侍郎，累遷散騎常侍、黃門郎、御史中丞。

translations.literal: Prince Jing Tian courtesy Yuanyu youth appointed irregular cavalry gentleman progressively irregular cavalry attendant yellow-gate gentleman palace Assistant chief.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Tian rose through palace attendant posts to censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 值海西廢，簡文帝登阼，未解嚴，大司馬桓溫屯中堂，吹警角，恬奏劾溫大不敬，請科罪。

translations.literal: When Haixi was deposed Emperor Jianwen ascended throne martial law not yet lifted Grand Marshal Huan Wen encamped Central Hall sounding alarm horns Tian memorialized impeaching Wen greatly irreverent requesting sentencing crime.
translations.idiomatic: Before demobilization Tian impeached Huan Wen's trumpet fanfare as lèse-majesté.

sentences.zh: 溫視奏歎曰：「此兒乃敢彈我，真可畏也。」

translations.literal: Wen viewing memorial sighed saying 'This lad dares impeach me—truly formidable.'
translations.idiomatic: Wen viewing memorial sighed saying 'This lad dares impeach me—truly formidable.'

title.zh: 卷九十四 列傳第六十四 隱逸
title.raw: 卷九十四 列傳第六十四 隱逸 Volume 94 Biographies 64: Hermits and Recluses

value.event: Summoned Meng Lou [External dating, inferred: Eastern Jin by conventional chronology.]

sentences.zh: 若夫穹昊垂景，少微以躔其次；

translations.literal: As for the vaulted heaven lowering its radiance, Shaowei thereby treads its place among them;
translations.idiomatic: Consider how the high heavens let fall their light, and the hermit star Shaowei keeps to its station in the sky.

sentences.zh: 《文》《系》探幽，貞遁以成其象。

translations.literal: The "Wen" and "Xi" plumb the hidden; steadfast withdrawal completes their image.
translations.idiomatic: The "Appended Remarks" and "Wings" sound out what lies in shadow, and the hexagram of principled retreat gives that stance its perfect emblem.

sentences.zh: 故有避於言色，其道聞乎孔公；

translations.literal: Therefore there were those who avoided it in speech and countenance; of their way one hears from the Duke Kong;
translations.idiomatic: Hence men who gave nothing away in word or look, whose path we know because Confucius spoke of them;

sentences.zh: 驕乎富貴，厥義詳于孫子。

translations.literal: As for pride toward wealth and noble rank, its meaning was set forth in detail by Master Sun.
translations.idiomatic: and the proud scorning of wealth and station, whose moral sense Sunzi laid out at length.

sentences.zh: 是以處柔伊存，有生之恆性；

translations.literal: Therefore to abide in softness is how it endures; it is the constant nature of the living;
translations.idiomatic: To hold to yielding strength is how life endures; that is the fixed temper of everything that breathes;

sentences.zh: 在盈斯害，惟神之常道。

translations.literal: to be at fullness is thereby harm; it is the constant way of the spirit.
translations.idiomatic: while fullness invites injury—such has always been heaven's steady law.

sentences.zh: 古先智士體其若茲，介焉超俗，浩然養素，藏聲江海之上，卷跡囂氛之表，漱流而激其清，寢巢而韜其耀，良畫以符其志，絕機以虛其心。

translations.literal: Ancient wise men embodied it thus: standing apart they transcended the vulgar, in vast purity they nurtured simplicity, they hid their voices above the rivers and seas, they rolled up their traces beyond the clamor and dust, they rinsed their mouths in the current to quicken its clearness, they slept in nests to sheathe their brilliance, they took fine plans to match their intent, they cut off contrivance to empty their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Men of old who grasped this truth stood aloof from the crowd, breathed in a clarity that nourished plain living, let their names die away beyond the rivers and seas, and withdrew their footsteps from the world's noise. They drank from running water to keep themselves clean, dwelt like birds in the wild to dim their luster, chose their course with deliberate care, and stilled every scheme so the heart could rest empty.

sentences.zh: 玉輝冰潔，川渟岳峙，修至樂之道，固無疆之休，長往邈而不追，安排窅而無悶，修身自保，悔吝弗生，詩人《考槃》之歌，抑在茲矣。

translations.literal: Jade radiance, ice purity; like a river at rest, like a peak standing; they cultivated the way of supreme joy, they secured boundless good fortune; long gone, remote, none could pursue them; settled in the depths, without vexation; they cultivated the self to preserve themselves, regret and shame did not arise—the poet's song of "Kao pan," is it not here?
translations.idiomatic: They shone like jade and held the chill of ice; they were still as a held river, steadfast as a mountain. They walked the path of deepest contentment and won a peace without end. Once they had gone far, none could overtake them; they accepted whatever came, untroubled in the dark. Guarding the person, they kept harm away—no cause for remorse—and the ode the Classic of Poetry calls "Kao pan" might almost have been written of them.

sentences.zh: 至於體天作制之後，訟息刑清之時，尚乃仄席幽貞以康神化，徵聘之禮賁於岩穴，玉帛之贄委於窒衡，故《月令》曰：「季春之月聘名士，禮賢者」，斯之謂歟！

translations.literal: As for after one embodied heaven and established institutions, at the time when lawsuits ceased and punishments were clear, still one vacated the mat for the hidden and steadfast to perfect spiritual transformation; the rites of summons and appointment shone into cliffside caves, gifts of jade and silk piled at humble doors—therefore the "Monthly Ordinances" says, "In the last month of spring one hires eminent scholars and treats the worthy with ritual"—does it not mean this?
translations.idiomatic: Even once a ruler had aligned his government with heaven and the courts fell quiet, he would still leave the high seat half-empty for recluses of firm integrity, so culture might flourish. Envoys climbed to mountain huts; jade and silk waited on the doorsteps of the poor. That is why the "Monthly Ordinances" says that in late spring one should call forth noted scholars and honor the wise—surely it speaks of just such a time.

sentences.zh: 自典午運開，旁求隱逸，譙元彥之杜絕人事，江思悛之嘯詠林藪，峻其貞白之軌，成其出塵之跡，雖不應其嘉招，亦足激其貪競。

translations.literal: From when the Jin fortune opened, seeking far and wide for recluses, as with Qiao Xiuyuan's cutting off human affairs, or Jiang Silun's whistling and chanting in woods and marshes, they made steep the track of chastity and purity, they completed traces beyond the dust; although they did not respond to fine summons, still it was enough to sting greed and rivalry.
translations.idiomatic: Since the house of Jin rose, the throne has combed the hills for hidden men: Qiao Xiu shut his gate on the world, Jiang Dun whistled and sang deep in the hills. They raised the standard of unstained integrity and showed how to step outside the scramble for power. They never took the court's gracious offers, yet their example was enough to shame the grasping and the ambitious.

sentences.zh: 今美其高尚之德，綴集於篇。

translations.literal: Now I praise their lofty virtue and string them together in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Here I gather their stories to honor the height of their character.

sentences.zh: 孟陋，字少孤，武昌人也。

translations.literal: Meng Lou, styled Shaogu, was a man of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Lou, courtesy name Shaogu, came from Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 吳司空宗之曾孫也。

translations.literal: He was great-grandson of Wu's minister of works Meng Zong.
translations.idiomatic: He was great-grandson of Wu minister Meng Zong.

sentences.zh: 兄嘉，桓溫征西長史。

translations.literal: His elder brother Meng Jia was chief clerk on Huan Wen's western campaign.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Meng Jia had been chief clerk under Huan Wen.

sentences.zh: 陋少而貞立，清操絕倫，布衣蔬食，以文籍自娛。

translations.literal: Lou in youth was chaste and established, his pure conduct unmatched, in plain cloth and coarse food, taking pleasure in books.
translations.idiomatic: Young, he was chaste, austere, in sackcloth and gruel, happy only in books.

sentences.zh: 口不及世事，未曾交遊，時或弋釣，孤興獨往，雖家人亦不知其所之也。

translations.literal: His mouth did not touch the affairs of the age; he never socialized; sometimes he shot or fished, alone with his whim—even his household did not know where he went.
translations.idiomatic: He never gossiped, rarely visited anyone, fished or hunted alone—his family never knew his path.

sentences.zh: 喪母，毀瘠殆於滅性，不飲酒食肉十有餘年。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he wasted his flesh almost to extinguishing nature; for more than ten years he drank no wine and ate no meat.
translations.idiomatic: His mother's death left him skeletal; he ate no meat over ten years.

sentences.zh: 親族迭謂之曰：「少孤！

translations.literal: Lineage kin in turn said to him, "Shaogu!
translations.idiomatic: Kinsmen pleaded, "Shaogu!

sentences.zh: 誰無父母？

translations.literal: Who lacks parents?
translations.idiomatic: Who has no parents?

sentences.zh: 誰有父母！

translations.literal: Who has parents!
translations.idiomatic: Who keeps parents forever?

sentences.zh: 聖人制禮，令賢者俯就，不肖企及。

translations.literal: The sages fixed ritual to let the worthy bend down and the unworthy strive up.
translations.idiomatic: The sages set rites so the wise may ease grief and fools may aim higher.

sentences.zh: 若使毀性無嗣，更為不孝也。」

translations.literal: If you destroy your nature and leave no heir, that is again unfilial.
translations.idiomatic: To die childless is the greater unfilial act."

sentences.zh: 陋感此言，然後從吉。

translations.literal: Lou was moved by these words; then afterward he followed auspicious rites.
translations.idiomatic: He heard them, relented, and ended mourning properly.

sentences.zh: 由是名著海內。

translations.literal: From this his name was famed within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: His name then filled the empire.

sentences.zh: 簡文帝輔政，命為參軍，稱疾不起。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jianwen assisted the government, he ordered him as adviser; he claimed illness and did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen summoned him as adviser; he pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 桓溫躬往造焉。

translations.literal: Huan Wen in person went to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen himself knocked on his door.

sentences.zh: 或謂溫曰：「孟陋高行，學為儒宗，宜引在府，以和鼎味。」

translations.literal: Someone said to Wen, "Meng Lou's conduct is lofty; his learning is patriarch of Confucians—it is fitting to draw him into the office to harmonize the cauldron's flavor."
translations.idiomatic: A friend told Huan Wen, 'Meng Lou's virtue tops the scholars; bring him to your staff to leaven the court.'

sentences.zh: 溫歎曰：「會稽王尚不能屈，非敢擬議也。」

translations.literal: Wen sighed, saying, "The prince of Kuaiji still could not bend him—how dare I presume to discuss it."
translations.idiomatic: Wen sighed, 'Even the prince of Kuaiji could not move him—I hardly dare speak of hiring him.'

sentences.zh: 陋聞之曰：「桓公正當以我不往故耳。

translations.literal: Lou heard it and said, "Lord Huan only thinks it is because I did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Lou heard and said, 'Huan Wen only thinks I snubbed him on purpose.

sentences.zh: 億兆之人，無官者十居其九，豈皆高士哉！

translations.literal: Of the myriad million men, nine in ten have no office—are they all lofty gentlemen!
translations.idiomatic: Nine men in ten lack office—are they all recluses?

sentences.zh: 我疾病不堪恭相王之命，非敢為高也。」

translations.literal: I am ill and cannot bear the respectful commands of the minister king—it is not that I dare be lofty."
translations.idiomatic: I am too sick to obey the prince's summons—that is no pose of pride.'

sentences.zh: 由是名稱益重。

translations.literal: From this his reputation and title grew heavier.
translations.idiomatic: His name only grew weightier after that.

sentences.zh: 博學多通，長於《三禮》。

translations.literal: He was broadly learned and penetrating, excelling in the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 注《論語》，行於世。

translations.literal: He annotated the Analects, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Analects commentary circulates still.

sentences.zh: 卒以壽終。

translations.literal: He ended his life at a full old age.
translations.idiomatic: He died in ripe old age.

title.zh: 卷一百〇一 載記第一 劉元海（劉淵） 劉宣
title.en: Volume 101 Records 1: Liu Yuanhai and Liu Xuan
title.raw: 卷一百〇一 載記第一 劉元海（劉淵） 劉宣 Volume 101 Records 1: Liu Yuanhai and Liu Xuan

meta.sourceNote: ChineseNotes page has no body text; imported chapter body from Wikisource.

sentences.zh: 劉元海（子和） 劉宣

translations.literal: Liu Yuanhai (son: He) and Liu Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuanhai (with his son He) and Liu Xuan.

translations.literal: (Son: He)
translations.idiomatic: (His son He)

sentences.zh: 劉宣

translations.literal: Liu Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuan.

sentences.zh: 東嬴公騰使將軍聶玄討之，戰於大陵，玄師敗績，騰懼，率并州二萬餘戶下山東，遂所在為寇。

translations.literal: Dongying Duke Teng sent General Nie Xuan to attack him; they fought at Daling; Xuan's army was routed; Teng, in fear, led more than twenty thousand households of Bingzhou down to Shandong, and thereupon everywhere became bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Teng sent Nie Xuan against him, lost at Daling, then fled Bing with twenty thousand families eastward, leaving the province to chaos.

sentences.zh: 元海遣其建武將軍劉曜寇太原、泫氏、屯留、長子、中都，皆陷之。

translations.literal: Yuanhai sent his General Who Establishes Might Liu Yao to raid Taiyuan, Xuan, Tunliu, Changzi, and Zhongdu—all fell.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan sent Liu Yao to storm Taiyuan, Xuan, Tunliu, Changzi, and Zhongdu—all fell.

sentences.zh: 二年，騰又遣司馬瑜、周良、石鮮等討之，次於離石汾城。

translations.literal: In the second year Teng again sent Sima Yu, Zhou Liang, Shi Xian, and others to attack him, halting at Fencheng of Lishi.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Sima Teng sent Sima Yu, Zhou Liang, and Shi Xian to Lishi's Fencheng.

sentences.zh: 元海遣其武牙將軍劉欽等六軍距瑜等，四戰，瑜皆敗，欽振旅而歸。

translations.literal: Yuanhai sent his General Who Martial Fangs Liu Qin and six armies to oppose Yu and the others; after four battles Yu was defeated each time, and Qin returned with drums beating.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan sent Liu Qin with six hosts; after four battles Jin fled and Liu Qin marched home in triumph.

sentences.zh: 是歲，離石大饑，遷于黎亭，以就邸閣穀，留其太尉劉宏、護軍馬景守離石，使大司農卜豫運糧以給之。

translations.literal: That year Lishi suffered great famine; they moved to Liting to draw on granary grain, leaving Grand Commandant Liu Hong and Protector Ma Jing to guard Lishi, and ordered Grand Minister of Agriculture Bu Yu to transport grain to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: Famine struck Lishi, so the court moved to Liting granaries while Liu Hong and Ma Jing held Lishi and Bu Yu shipped grain.

sentences.zh: 以其前將軍劉景為使持節、征討大都督、大將軍，要擊并州刺史劉琨于版橋，為琨所敗，琨遂據晉陽。

translations.literal: He made his former general Liu Jing credential-holder, grand commander for conquest, grand general, and intercepted Bing Governor Liu Kun at Banqiao; he was defeated by Kun, and Kun thereupon occupied Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Liu Jing to ambush Liu Kun at Banqiao; Liu Kun crushed him and took Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 其侍中劉殷、王育進諫元海曰：「殿下自起兵以來，漸已一周，而顓守偏方，王威未震。

translations.literal: His attendants Liu Yin and Wang Yu advanced remonstrance to Yuanhai, saying, "Since Your Highness raised troops it has gradually been a full cycle, yet you only hold a corner; kingly awe has not yet shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin and Wang Yu urged him: "A year has passed and you still hug one corner—your majesty has not yet thundered abroad.

sentences.zh: 誠能命將四出，決機一擲，梟劉琨，定河東，建帝號，鼓行而南，克長安而都之，以關中之眾席捲洛陽，如指掌耳。

translations.literal: If you truly can order generals to go out on four sides, cast the die once, behead Liu Kun, settle Hedong, establish an imperial title, beat the drum southward, take Chang'an as capital, then with the hosts of Guanzhong roll up Luoyang—it is like turning the palm.
translations.idiomatic: Send four columns, kill Liu Kun, secure Hedong, proclaim the throne, march on Chang'an, then sweep from the passes to Luoyang like turning your hand.

sentences.zh: 此高皇帝之所以創啟鴻基，克殄強楚者也。」

translations.literal: This is how the High Emperor opened the great foundation and utterly destroyed mighty Chu."
translations.idiomatic: That was Gaozu's road to crush Chu."

sentences.zh: 元海悅曰：「此孤心也。」

translations.literal: Yuanhai, pleased, said, "This is Our heart."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan cried, "That is my own mind too."

sentences.zh: 遂進據河東，攻寇蒲阪、平陽，皆陷之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he advanced and occupied Hedong, attacked and raided Puyin and Pingyang, and both fell.
translations.idiomatic: He drove into Hedong, stormed Puyin and Pingyang, and took both.

sentences.zh: 元海遂入都蒲子，河東、平陽屬縣壘壁盡降。

translations.literal: Yuanhai thereupon entered and made his capital at Puzi; fortified camps of the counties of Hedong and Pingyang all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He moved the capital to Puzi; every fort in Hedong and Pingyang opened its gates.

sentences.zh: 時汲桑起兵趙魏，上郡四部鮮卑陸逐延、氏酋大單于征、東萊王彌及石勒等並相次降之，元海悉署其官爵，

translations.literal: At that time Ji Sang raised troops in Zhao and Wei; Lüzhuyan of the four Xianbei sections of Shangjun, Di chief Great-Shanyu Zheng, Wang Mi of Donglai, and Shi Le in succession each surrendered to him; Yuanhai all appointed their offices and noble ranks,
translations.idiomatic: Ji Sang rose in Zhao-Wei; Xianbei, Di, Wang Mi, and Shi Le came over in turn; Liu Yuan handed each a title.

value.descriptorSuggestion: Rui's son enthroned by Huan Wen

sentences.zh: 昔黃帝有子二十五人，或內列諸華，或外分荒服，昌意少子，受封北土，國有大鮮卑山，因以為號。

translations.literal: In olden times the Yellow Emperor had twenty-five sons; some were enrolled within the Chinese domains, some were apportioned to distant borderlands. Changyi was his youngest son; he received a fief in the northern lands. The state had the great Xianbei Mountain, and from it took its name.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago the Yellow Emperor had twenty-five sons: some served within the Chinese heartland, others were sent to govern the outer marches. Changyi, his youngest, was enfeoffed in the north, where the great Xianbei Mountain stood—and from that mountain the people took their name.

sentences.zh: 其後，世為君長，統幽都之北，廣漠之野，畜牧遷徙，射獵為業，淳樸為俗，簡易為化，不為文字，刻木紀契而已，世事遠近，人相傳授，如史官之紀錄焉。

translations.literal: Thereafter generation after generation they were chieftains, ruling north of Youdu in the vast deserts. Pastoral migration and hunting were their livelihood; simplicity their custom, plainness their transformation. They did not use writing, but only carved wood to record agreements. Affairs near and far were passed from person to person, like the records of historians.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward they ruled generation upon generation north of Youdu, across the wide steppe. They lived by herding, moving with the seasons, and by the hunt; their ways were plain, their customs unadorned. They had no script—only notches cut in wood to seal bargains. What happened near and far was handed down mouth to mouth, much as if scribes had kept annals.

sentences.zh: 黃帝以土德王，北俗謂土為托，謂后為跋，故以為氏。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor ruled by the virtue of Earth; in northern custom earth was called tuo and a queen was called ba, hence they took it as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor reigned under the virtue of Earth; northerners called earth tuo and called a queen ba—so the clan took the name Tuoba.

sentences.zh: 其裔始均，入仕堯世，逐女魃於弱水之北，民賴其勤，帝舜嘉之，命為田祖。

translations.literal: His descendant Shijun entered service in the age of Yao, drove Nüba north of the Weak Water; the people relied on his diligence, Emperor Shun praised him, and appointed him Lord of the Fields.
translations.idiomatic: A descendant, Shijun, served in the reign of Yao, driving the drought demon Nüba beyond the Weak Water. The people owed their relief to his labor; Shun commended him and named him Lord of the Fields.

sentences.zh: 爰歷三代，以及秦漢，獯鬻、獫狁、山戎、匈奴之屬，累代殘暴，作害中州，而始均之裔，不交南夏，是以載籍無聞焉。

translations.literal: Thus through the Three Dynasties down to Qin and Han, the Xunyu, Xianyun, Shanrong, Xiongnu and their kind were generation after generation violent, harming the Central States—but the descendants of Shijun did not mingle with Southern Xia, and therefore they go unmentioned in written records.
translations.idiomatic: Through the Three Dynasties and on into Qin and Han, the Xiongnu and their kindred peoples—Xunyu, Xianyun, Shanrong—ravaged the Central Plains generation after generation. Yet Shijun's line never dealt with the southern realms, and so the written histories say nothing of them.

sentences.zh: 三十四年春，長孫斤謀反，伏誅。

translations.literal: In the spring of the thirty-fourth year Changsun Jin plotted rebellion and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the thirty-fourth year Changsun Jin plotted rebellion and was executed.

sentences.zh: 斤之反也，拔刃向御座，太子獻明皇帝諱寔格之，傷脅。

translations.literal: When Jin rebelled he drew his blade toward the imperial seat; the crown prince, the future Emperor Xianming, taboo name Shi, blocked him and was wounded in the flank.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin rebelled he drew his blade toward the throne; the crown prince—the future Emperor Xianming, taboo name Shi—blocked him and was wounded in the flank.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，薨，後追諡焉。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer he died; posthumous title was conferred afterward.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer he died; a posthumous title was conferred later.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，皇孫珪生，大赦。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn the imperial grandson Gui was born; a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn the imperial grandson Gui was born, and a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 是年，司馬弈臣桓溫，廢弈為海西公，立叡子昱。

translations.literal: That year the minister Sima Yi's subject Huan Wen deposed Yi as Prince of Haixi and installed Rui's son Yu.
translations.idiomatic: That year Sima Yi's subject Huan Wen deposed Yi as Prince of Haixi and enthroned Rui's son Yu.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，司馬昱死，子昌明僭立。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year Sima Yu died; his son Changming usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year Sima Yu died, and his son Changming usurped the throne.

bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

value.descriptorSuggestion: Prince of Qin, son of Sima Yun

value.event: Sima Yu, Prince of Qin, was killed with his father Sima Yun

value.statement: Sima Yu, Prince of Qin, was killed

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑第083卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Government, Volume 83
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 83

sentences.zh: 中護軍淮南王允，性沉毅，宿衛將士皆畏服之。

translations.literal: The Central Protector of the Army, the Prince of Huainan Yun, was by nature deep and resolute; the garrison soldiers all feared and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yun, Prince of Huainan, Central Protector of the Army, was deep and resolute by nature, and the palace guards all feared him.

sentences.zh: 允知相國倫及孫秀有異志，陰養死士，謀討之；

translations.literal: Yun knew Chancellor Lun and Sun Xiu harbored rebellious intent and secretly nurtured men willing to die, plotting to attack them;
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Lun and Xiu meant to rebel, he secretly gathered men willing to die and plotted against them;

sentences.zh: 倫、秀深憚之。

translations.literal: Lun and Xiu deeply dreaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Lun and Xiu feared him deeply.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，轉允為太尉，外示優崇，實奪其兵權。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, Yun was transferred to Grand Commandant—outwardly a mark of honor, in reality his military power was taken away.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, he was transferred to Grand Commandant, an outward honor that in fact stripped him of military command.

sentences.zh: 允稱疾不拜。

translations.literal: Yun pleaded illness and would not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and refused the appointment.

sentences.zh: 秀遣御史劉機逼允，收其官屬以下，劾以拒詔，大逆不敬。

translations.literal: Xiu sent the Censor Liu Ji to press Yun, seized his officials and subordinates, and impeached him for resisting an edict, great irreverence and impiety.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu sent Censor Liu Ji to coerce him, arrested his staff, and charged him with resisting an edict and great impiety.

sentences.zh: 允視詔，乃秀手書也，大怒，收御史，將斬之，御史走免，斬其令史二人。

translations.literal: Yun looked at the edict—it was in Xiu's own hand—and grew greatly angry, seized the censor, and was about to behead him; the censor fled and escaped, and two clerks were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Yun saw the edict was in Xiu's own hand, flew into a rage, seized the censor and nearly executed him; the censor fled, and two clerks were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 厲色謂左右曰：「趙王欲破我家！」

translations.literal: With stern countenance he said to those at his side: "The Prince of Zhao means to destroy my house!"
translations.idiomatic: He said grimly to his attendants: "The Prince of Zhao means to destroy my house!"

sentences.zh: 遂帥國兵及帳下七百人直出，大呼曰：「趙王反，我將討之，從我者左袒。」

translations.literal: He thereupon led his state troops and seven hundred men of his personal guard straight out, shouting loudly: "The Prince of Zhao has rebelled—I shall punish him; those who follow me, bare your left shoulder."
translations.idiomatic: He led his state troops and seven hundred household guards straight out, shouting: "The Prince of Zhao has rebelled! I shall punish him. Follow me and bare your left shoulder."

sentences.zh: 於是歸之者甚眾。

translations.literal: At this very many came over to him.
translations.idiomatic: Many rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 允將赴宮，尚書左丞王輿閉掖門，允不得入，遂圍相府。

translations.literal: Yun was about to go to the palace; the Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Yu closed the side gate, and Yun could not enter; he thereupon besieged the chancellor's mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Yun marched on the palace, but Wang Yu, Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, shut the side gate and blocked him; he then besieged the chancellor's residence.

sentences.zh: 允所將兵皆精銳，倫與戰，屢敗，死者千餘人。

translations.literal: The troops Yun led were all elite; Lun fought him and was repeatedly defeated, more than a thousand dead.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's troops were elite. Lun fought him repeatedly and lost, with more than a thousand dead.

sentences.zh: 太子左率陳徽勒東宮兵，鼓噪於內以應允。

translations.literal: Chen Hui, Colonel of the Left Guards of the Heir Apparent, roused Eastern Palace troops and clamored within in support of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hui, Colonel of the Left Guards of the Heir Apparent, stirred Eastern Palace troops to cheer within in support of Yun.

sentences.zh: 允結陳於承華門前，弓弩齊發，射倫，飛矢雨下。

translations.literal: Yun drew up his array before the Chenghua Gate; bows and crossbows fired together, shooting at Lun—arrows fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: Yun formed battle lines before the Chenghua Gate. Bows and crossbows volleyed at Lun until arrows fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 主書司馬眭秘以身蔽倫，箭中其背而死。

translations.literal: The Chief Clerk Sima Sui shielded Lun with his body; an arrow struck his back and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Sima Sui shielded Lun with his body and was killed by an arrow in the back.

sentences.zh: 倫官屬皆隱樹而立，每樹輒中數百箭，自辰至未，中書令陳淮，徽之兄也，欲應允，言於帝曰：「宜遣白虎幡以解鬥。」

translations.literal: Lun's staff all hid behind trees to stand; each tree received hundreds of arrows. From the hour chen to wei, the Secretariat Director Chen Huai—Hui's elder brother—wished to support Yun and said to the emperor: "The white tiger banner should be sent to halt the fighting."
translations.idiomatic: Lun's staff hid behind trees, each tree studded with hundreds of arrows. From chen to wei, Chen Huai, Secretariat Director and Hui's elder brother, wished to aid Yun and told the emperor: "Send the white tiger banner to stop the fighting."

sentences.zh: 乃使司馬督護伏胤將騎四百持幡從宮中出。

translations.literal: He then had the Major Fu Yin of the Protectorate lead four hundred horsemen bearing the banner out from within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Major of the Protectorate Fu Yin was sent with four hundred horsemen bearing the banner from the palace.

sentences.zh: 侍中汝陰王虔在門下省，陰與胤誓曰：「富貴當與卿共之。」

translations.literal: The Attendant, the Prince of Runan Qian, was in the Gate Department; he secretly swore with Yin: "Wealth and honor shall be shared with you."
translations.idiomatic: The Attendant, Prince of Runan Qian, was in the Gate Department and secretly swore to Yin: "We shall share wealth and honor."

sentences.zh: 胤乃懷空板出，詐言有詔助淮南王。

translations.literal: Yin then carried a blank tablet out and falsely said there was an edict to aid the Prince of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Yin carried out a blank tablet and falsely claimed an edict to aid the Prince of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 允不之覺，開陣內之，下車受詔；

translations.literal: Yun did not perceive the deception and opened his ranks to admit him; Yun dismounted to receive the edict;
translations.idiomatic: Yun did not detect the fraud and opened his ranks. Yun dismounted to receive the edict;

sentences.zh: 胤因殺之，並殺允子秦王郁、漢王迪，坐允夷滅者數千人。

translations.literal: Yin thereupon killed him, and also killed Yun's sons, the Prince of Qin Yu and the Prince of Han Di; those implicated with Yun and exterminated numbered several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yin then killed him, along with Yun's sons Yu, Prince of Qin, and Di, Prince of Han. Several thousand connected with Yun were exterminated.

sentences.zh: 曲赦洛陽。

translations.literal: A partial amnesty was granted to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: A partial amnesty was granted to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 初，孫秀嘗為小吏，事黃門郎潘岳，岳屢撻之。

translations.literal: Earlier Sun Xiu had once been a petty clerk serving the Yellow Gate Gentleman Pan Yue; Yue often flogged him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xiu had served as a petty clerk under Pan Yue, Yellow Gate Gentleman, who had often flogged him.

sentences.zh: 衛尉石崇之甥歐陽建素與相國倫有隙，崇有愛妾曰綠珠，孫秀便求之，崇不與。

translations.literal: Ouyang Jian, nephew of the Commandant of the Guards Shi Chong, had long been at odds with Chancellor Lun; Chong had a beloved concubine named Green Pearl whom Sun Xiu asked for, but Chong would not give her.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Jian, nephew of Commandant of the Guards Shi Chong, was estranged from Lun. Chong had a beloved concubine, Green Pearl, whom Xiu demanded and Chong refused.

sentences.zh: 及淮南王允敗，秀因稱石崇、潘岳、歐陽建奉允為亂，收之。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Huainan Yun was defeated, Xiu thereupon claimed that Shi Chong, Pan Yue, and Ouyang Jian supported Yun in rebellion and arrested them.
translations.idiomatic: When Yun fell, Xiu accused Chong, Yue, and Jian of supporting his rebellion and arrested them.

sentences.zh: 崇歎曰：「奴輩利吾財爾！」

translations.literal: Chong sighed: "These slaves covet my wealth!"
translations.idiomatic: Chong sighed: "These slaves want my wealth!"

sentences.zh: 收者曰：「知財為禍，何不早散之？」

translations.literal: The arresters said: "Knowing wealth brings disaster, why not have dispersed it early?"
translations.idiomatic: The arresters said: "If wealth brings disaster, why not have given it away?"

sentences.zh: 崇不能答。

translations.literal: Chong could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Chong had no answer.

sentences.zh: 初，潘岳母常誚責岳曰：「汝當知足，而乾沒不已乎！」

translations.literal: Earlier Pan Yue's mother often reproached Yue, saying: "You ought to know sufficiency—why seize and scrape without end!"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yue's mother had often scolded him: "Know when you have enough—why keep grasping for more?"

sentences.zh: 及敗，岳謝母曰：「負阿母。」

translations.literal: When disaster came Yue apologized to his mother: "I have failed you, Mother."
translations.idiomatic: When ruin came Yue told his mother: "I have failed you, Mother."

sentences.zh: 遂與崇，建皆族誅，籍沒崇家。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yue, Chong, and Jian were all executed to the clan, and Chong's property was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Yue, Chong, and Jian were executed to the clan, and Chong's estate was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 相國倫收淮南王母弟吳王晏，欲殺之。

translations.literal: Chancellor Lun arrested the Prince of Wu Yan, the Prince of Huainan's younger brother by the same mother, intending to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Lun arrested Yan, Prince of Wu, Yun's younger brother by the same mother, intending to kill him.

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫傅祗爭之於朝堂，眾皆諫止倫，倫乃貶晏為賓徒縣王。

translations.literal: The Household Grandee Fu Zhi contended for him in the court hall; all remonstrated and stopped Lun, and Lun thereupon degraded Yan to Prince of Bintu county.
translations.idiomatic: Household Grandee Fu Zhi argued for him in court; all remonstrated, and Lun degraded Yan to Prince of Bintu.

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第097卷

translations.literal: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 97.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 97.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，乙卯，帝不豫；

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on yǐmǎo, the emperor fell ill;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fifth month, on yǐmǎo, the emperor fell gravely ill;

sentences.zh: 六月，庚寅，疾篤。

translations.literal: in the sixth month, on gēngyín, his illness became critical.
translations.idiomatic: and in the sixth month, on gēngyín, his condition turned critical.

sentences.zh: 或詐為尚書符，敕宮門無得內宰相；

translations.literal: Someone forged an order in the name of the Secretariat forbidding the palace gates to admit the chief ministers;
translations.idiomatic: Someone forged a Secretariat order barring chief ministers from entering the palace gates;

sentences.zh: 眾皆失色。

translations.literal: all turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: and everyone turned pale with alarm.

sentences.zh: 庾冰曰：「此必詐也。」

translations.literal: Yu Bing said, "This must be a fraud."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bing said, "This must be a forgery."

sentences.zh: 推問，果然。

translations.literal: On investigation, it proved so.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation proved that it was.

sentences.zh: 帝二子丕、弈，皆在襁褓。

translations.literal: The emperor's two sons Pi and Yi were both still in swaddling clothes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's two sons, Pi and Yi, were both still infants.

sentences.zh: 庾冰自以兄弟秉權日久，恐易世之後，親屬愈疏，為它人所間，每說帝以國有強敵，宜立長君；

translations.literal: Yu Bing, considering that he and his brothers had held power long, feared that after a change of reign kinsmen would grow more distant and others would drive wedges between them; he repeatedly urged the emperor that with powerful enemies abroad the state should install an elder sovereign;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bing, knowing that he and his brothers had held power for years, feared that after a change of reign their kin would be pushed aside and others would come between them; he repeatedly urged the emperor that with powerful foes abroad the throne should pass to a mature heir.

sentences.zh: 請以母親弟琅邪王岳為嗣，帝許之。

translations.literal: he asked that the emperor's younger maternal half-brother, Prince of Langye Yue, be made heir, and the emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed the emperor's younger uterine half-brother, Prince Yue of Langye, as successor, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 中書令何充曰：「父子相傳，先王舊典，易之者鮮不致亂。

translations.literal: Zhongshu Ling He Chong said, "Father-to-son succession is the ancient royal norm; those who change it rarely escape disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He Chong, Director of the Secretariat, said, "Passing the throne from father to son is the ancient royal norm; those who alter it seldom avoid turmoil.

sentences.zh: 故武王不授聖弟，非不愛也。

translations.literal: Therefore King Wu did not give the throne to his sage younger brother—not from lack of love.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu did not enthrone his gifted younger brother—not because he loved him less.

sentences.zh: 今琅邪踐阼，將如孺子何！」

translations.literal: If Langye now ascends the throne, what is to become of the infant sons!"
translations.idiomatic: If Prince Langye takes the throne, what will become of these infant princes!"

sentences.zh: 冰不聽。

translations.literal: Bing would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Bing would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 下詔，以岳為嗣，並以弈繼琅邪哀王。

translations.literal: An edict was issued making Yue the heir and also assigning Yi to succeed the late Prince Ai of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: An edict named Yue as heir and assigned Yi to succeed the late Prince Ai of Langye.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，冰、充及武陵王晞、會稽王昱、尚書令諸葛恢並受顧命。

translations.literal: On rénchén, Bing, Chong, Prince Xi of Wuling, Prince Yu of Kuaiji, and Shangshu Ling Zhuge Hui all received the dying emperor's charge.
translations.idiomatic: On rénchén, Bing, Chong, Prince Xi of Wuling, Prince Yu of Kuaiji, and Zhuge Hui, Director of the Secretariat, all received the emperor's deathbed commission.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，帝崩。

translations.literal: On guǐsì, the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: On guǐsì the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 帝幼沖嗣位，不親庶政；

translations.literal: The emperor had succeeded young and did not personally handle routine government;
translations.idiomatic: He had come to the throne as a child and had not personally directed routine affairs;

sentences.zh: 及長，頗有勤儉之德。

translations.literal: when he grew up he showed considerable virtue in diligence and frugality.
translations.idiomatic: but as he matured he showed real virtue in diligence and frugality.

sentences.zh: 帝疾篤，庾冰、庾翼欲立會稽王昱為嗣；

translations.literal: The emperor was gravely ill; Yu Bing and Yu Yi wished to install Prince Kuaiji of Kuaiji as heir;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was gravely ill; Yu Bing and Yu Yi wished to install Prince Kuaiji of Kuaiji as heir;

sentences.zh: 中書監何充建議立皇子聃，帝從之。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat He Chong proposed installing the imperial son Dan, and the emperor followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat He Chong proposed installing the imperial son Dan, and the emperor followed him.

sentences.zh: 九月，丙申，立聃為皇太子。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on bingchen, Dan was installed as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on bingchen, Dan was installed as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，帝崩於式乾殿。

translations.literal: On wuxu the emperor died in Shigan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu the emperor died in Shigan Hall.

sentences.zh: 己亥，何充以遺旨奉太子即位，大赦。

translations.literal: On jihai He Chong, by the late emperor's testament, installed the crown prince and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai He Chong, by the late emperor's testament, installed the crown prince and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 由是冰、翼深恨充。

translations.literal: From this Bing and Yi deeply resented Chong.
translations.idiomatic: From this Bing and Yi deeply resented Chong.

sentences.zh: 尊皇后褚氏為皇太后。

translations.literal: The empress of the Chu clan was honored as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The empress of the Chu clan was honored as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 時穆帝方二歲，太后臨朝稱制。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Mu was just two years old; the empress dowager held court and ruled in her own name.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Emperor Mu was just two years old; the empress dowager held court and ruled in her own name.

sentences.zh: 何充加中書監，錄尚書事。

translations.literal: He Chong was additionally made Director of the Secretariat with authority to record Masters of Writing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He Chong was additionally made director of the Secretariat with authority to record Masters of Writing affairs.

sentences.zh: 充自陳既錄尚書，不宜復監中書；

translations.literal: Chong himself stated that having authority to record the Masters of Writing, he ought not again to oversee the Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Chong himself stated that having authority to record Masters of Writing affairs, he ought not again to oversee the Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 許之，復加侍中。

translations.literal: this was granted, and he was additionally made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: this was granted, and he was additionally made palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 詔征衛將軍褚裒，欲以為揚州刺史、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: An edict summoned Defender-General Chu Pou, intending to make him Governor of Yangzhou and Recorder of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned Defender-General Chu Pou, intending to appoint him Governor of Yangzhou and Recorder of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書劉遐、長史王胡之說裒曰：「會稽王令德雅望，國之周公也，足下宜以大政授之。」

translations.literal: Minister of the Civil Service Liu Xia and Chief Clerk Wang Huzhi urged Pou, saying: "The Prince of Kuaiji's virtue and elegant reputation make him the Duke of Zhou of the state; you ought to entrust great affairs to him."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the Civil Service Liu Xia and chief clerk Wang Huzhi urged Pou: "The Prince of Kuaiji's virtue and reputation make him the state's Duke of Zhou; you ought to entrust supreme authority to him."

sentences.zh: 裒乃固辭，歸籓。

translations.literal: Pou then firmly declined and returned to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: Pou then firmly declined and returned to his fief.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，以會稽王昱為撫軍大將軍，錄尚書六條事。

translations.literal: On renxu, the Prince of Kuaiji, Sima Yu, was made General of Agitating the Army and Recorder of Six Articles of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu the Prince of Kuaiji, Sima Yu, was made General of Agitating the Army and Recorder of the Six Secretariat Articles.

sentences.zh: 昱清虛寡慾，尤善玄言，常以劉惔、王濛及穎川韓伯為談客，又辟郗超為撫軍掾，謝萬為從事中郎。

translations.literal: Yu was pure and sparing of desires, especially skilled in Dark Learning; he often took Liu Tan, Wang Meng, and Yingchuan's Han Bo as conversation guests; he also appointed Xi Chao as staff officer of the Agitating Army and Xie Wan as Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was pure and sparing of desire, especially skilled in Dark Learning; he often took Liu Tan, Wang Meng, and Han Bo of Yingchuan as conversationalists, and also appointed Xi Chao as staff officer of the Agitating Army and Xie Wan as Secretariat Attendant.

sentences.zh: 超，鑒之孫也，少卓犖不羈。

translations.literal: Chao was the grandson of Xi Jian; in youth he was outstanding and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Chao was Xi Jian's grandson; in youth he was outstanding and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 父愔，簡默沖退而嗇於財，積錢至數千萬，嘗開庫任超所取；

translations.literal: His father Xi Yin was plain, silent, retiring, and stingy with wealth, amassing cash to tens of millions; he once opened the treasury and let Chao take as he wished;
translations.idiomatic: His father Xi Yin was plain, silent, retiring, and miserly, amassing cash to tens of millions; he once opened the treasury and let Chao take as he wished;

sentences.zh: 超散施親故，一日都盡。

translations.literal: Chao distributed it to kin and friends and in one day spent it all.
translations.idiomatic: Chao distributed it to kin and friends and in a single day spent it all.

sentences.zh: 萬，安之弟也，清曠秀邁，亦有時名。

translations.literal: Wan was the younger brother of Xie An; pure, open, and elegantly lofty, he too had a name of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Wan was Xie An's younger brother—pure, open, and elegantly lofty—and he too enjoyed a reputation of the day.

sentences.zh: 丹楊尹劉惔每奇溫才，然知其有不臣之志，謂會稽王昱曰：「溫不可使居形勝之地，其位號常宜抑之。」

translations.literal: Governor of Danyang Liu Tan often marveled at Wen's talent, yet knew he harbored unruly ambitions; he told the Prince of Kuaiji, Sima Yu: "Wen must not be placed in a strategically decisive region; his rank and title should constantly be kept down."
translations.idiomatic: Governor of Danyang Liu Tan often marveled at Wen's talent, yet knew he harbored disloyal ambitions; he told the Prince of Kuaiji: "Wen must not be placed in a strategically decisive post; his rank and title should constantly be held down."

sentences.zh: 勸昱自鎮上流，以己為軍司，昱不聽；

translations.literal: He urged Yu personally to guard the upper reaches, with Tan himself as army marshal; Yu would not listen;
translations.idiomatic: He urged Yu personally to guard the upper reaches, with Tan himself as army marshal; Yu would not listen;

sentences.zh: 又請自行，亦不聽。

translations.literal: he asked again to go himself—again Yu would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: He asked again to go himself—again Yu would not listen.

sentences.zh: 二月，癸丑，以左光祿大夫蔡謨領司徒，與會稽王昱同輔政。

translations.literal: Second month, on guichou, Left Household Grandee Cai Mo was made acting Minister of Education, jointly assisting government with the Prince of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on guichou, Left Household Grandee Cai Mo was made acting Minister of Education, to assist government jointly with the Prince of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 褚裒薦前光祿大夫顧和、前司徒左長史殷浩；

translations.literal: Chu Pou recommended former Household Grandee Gu He and former Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education Yin Hao;
translations.idiomatic: Chu Pou recommended former Household Grandee Gu He and former left chief clerk of the Minister of Education Yin Hao;

sentences.zh: 三月，丙子，以和為尚書令，浩為建武將軍、揚州刺史。

translations.literal: Third month, on bingzi, He was made Director of the Secretariat and Hao made General of Establishing Martial Prowess and Governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on bingzi, He was made Director of the Secretariat and Hao General of Establishing Martial Prowess and Governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 和有母喪，固辭不起，謂所親曰：「古人有釋衰絰從王者，以其才足干時故也。

translations.literal: He was in mourning for his mother and firmly declined to take office; he told those close to him: "In antiquity some cast off mourning bands to follow kings because their talent sufficed to sustain the age.
translations.idiomatic: He was in mourning for his mother and firmly declined office; he told those close to him: "In antiquity some cast off mourning bands to follow kings because their talent sufficed to sustain the age.

sentences.zh: 如和者，正足以虧孝道、傷風俗耳。」

translations.literal: One like He would only enough to impair filial duty and harm custom."
translations.idiomatic: One like me would only impair filial duty and harm custom."

sentences.zh: 識者美之。

translations.literal: Those of insight praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Those of insight praised him.

sentences.zh: 浩亦固辭。

translations.literal: Hao also firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Hao also firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 會稽王昱與浩書曰：「屬當厄運，危弊理極，足下沈識淹長，足以經濟。

translations.literal: The Prince of Kuaiji, Sima Yu, wrote to Hao: "We face ill fortune; peril and decay have reached their limit. You have profound knowledge and long experience, enough to sustain the state.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Kuaiji wrote to Hao: "We face ill fortune; peril and decay have reached their limit. Your profound knowledge and long experience are enough to sustain the state.

sentences.zh: 若復深存挹退，苟遂本懷，吾恐天下之事於此去矣。

translations.literal: If you again deeply preserve modest withdrawal and simply follow your original wish, I fear the affairs of the realm at this point will pass away.
translations.idiomatic: If you again deeply preserve modest withdrawal and simply follow your original wish, I fear the realm's affairs will slip away at this very moment.

sentences.zh: 足下去就，即時之廢興，則家國不異，足下宜深思之。」

translations.literal: Your going or staying at this moment is the rise or fall of the age; then family and state are not different—you should ponder this deeply."
translations.idiomatic: Your going or staying at this moment is the rise or fall of the age; family and state are one—you should ponder this deeply."

sentences.zh: 浩乃就職。

translations.literal: Hao then took office.
translations.idiomatic: Hao then took office.
